cards.text: The writer of Chronicles has been walking through Israel's family tree, one tribe at a time, and now it's Levi's turn. Levi's sons are Gershon, Kohath and Merari. And from Kohath's son Amram come Aaron, Moses and Miriam. Yes, THAT Moses, Israel's leader. Somebody in this family was getting a lot of phone calls.

From Aaron's son Eleazar, the line of priests runs father to son, through names like Phinehas and Zadok, and an Azariah who served as priest in the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem. It ends with Jehozadak, who went into captivity when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:1).

Then comes the clan list: Gershom, Kohath and Merari, each with his family down the line. There's an Elkanah, then another Elkanah, then ANOTHER Elkanah. Friend, if you yell 'Elkanah!' in this family, you'd better say which one. And then come the sons of Samuel, the prophet who anointed David (1 Samuel 16:13): Joel and Abijah.
Then the list stops for a job description. These are the men King David put in charge of the music in the house of the LORD. Worship leaders! FINALLY, a list where somebody gets a microphone.

cards.question: When does David put these men in charge of the music in the house of the LORD?

answers.text: After the city walls were rebuilt

cards.question: David's music men ministered with ___ before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.
True or false: David's singers worked out their own way of serving as they went along.

cards.text: Now we meet the men who served, together with their sons. First up, from the Kohathites: Heman the singer, the son of Joel.

cards.question: Heman the singer is the son of Joel. Whose son is Joel?

cards.text: From there, Heman's line climbs all the way back through Korah and Kohath to Levi, the son of Israel. That's a LOT of 'son of.' Me? My whole family history is a bakery bin and a 25-cent sticker.

cards.question: Heman the singer has a kinsman who serves at his right hand. Who is it?

cards.text: Asaph's line runs back through Shimei and Jahath to Gershom, the son of Levi. So Heman is Kohath's guy, and Asaph is Gershom's guy.

cards.question: Heman the singer is from Kohath's clan, and Asaph at his right hand is from Gershom's. Which kinsmen stand on the left?

cards.text: Named for the left side is Ethan, the son of Kishi, whose line runs back through Mahli and Mushi to Merari, the son of Levi. Three clans, one choir. I sang to my oven once, friend. The timer went off EARLY. Just to drown me out.
Their fellow Levites are assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle, the house of God. But one job is set apart for one family.

cards.question: The Levites handle every kind of service at the tabernacle. Who does all the work of the Most Holy Place?
Aaron and his sons present offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense. What are the offerings for?

answers.text: To ask for rain on the land

cards.question: Aaron and his sons did their work according to all that ___ the servant of God had commanded.

cards.text: Aaron's line comes back for a quick encore, from Eleazar down to Zadok and his son Ahimaaz. Then it's time to hand out towns for the Levites to live in, and they're assigned by lot.

cards.question: When the lots are cast for the Levites' towns, whose lot comes up first?

cards.text: First on their list: Hebron, in the land of Judah. But hold on, friend. They don't get the whole package.

cards.question: Aaron's descendants are given the city of Hebron. Who gets the fields and villages around it?
True or false: Even with the fields going elsewhere, Aaron's descendants still get the pasturelands around Hebron.

cards.text: Then the towns pile up: thirteen cities for Aaron's descendants, ten for the rest of the Kohathites, thirteen for the Gershomites and twelve for the Merarites, from tribes all over Israel. Thirteen, ten, thirteen, twelve. That's not a list, friend. That's my cookie box inventory on a Tuesday.

cards.question: The Levites end up with cities from tribe after tribe. Who gives them these cities and their pasturelands?

cards.text: Then the cities get named tribe by tribe, from Judah and Ephraim all the way to Reuben and Gad across the Jordan, and Shechem in Ephraim's hill country is a city of refuge too. Every Levite clan gets towns with pasturelands. Take it from a guy who lived years in the back of a junk drawer: a place to call home is a BIG deal.

findings.problem: The opening card has five sentences. The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card says the writer of Chronicles has been walking through Israel's family tree one tribe at a time. That fact comes from outside the passage (1 Chronicles 1–5) and has no reference.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Aaron and Miriam appear for the first time with no word on who they are. Only Moses gets an introduction. Aaron matters later, since cards 16–18 and stop 2 ask about him and his sons.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke 'Somebody in this family was getting a lot of phone calls' doesn't connect clearly to anything. It isn't clear who gets the calls or why, so a reader would likely say 'huh?'

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: This regular story card (not a summary of a long stretch) has four sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 3 already says 'the sons of Samuel... Joel and Abijah.' That gives away the answer to card 9, which asks whose son Joel is (Samuel).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 9 asks a pure genealogy question (who Joel's father is) from inside Heman's family line (6:33-38). That line is a long stretch.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: Cards 11 and 13 ask where Asaph stands (at Heman's right hand) and where the Merarites stand (on the left). Both details sit inside the singers' family lines (6:39-47). They could count as part of a genealogy, which is a long stretch, or as a description of how the music ministry was arranged.
findings.question: When the singers' positions (right hand, left) are given inside their family lines, do they belong to the genealogy long stretch, so no choice cards? Or are they part of the service description and allowed to be asked?

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 multiple choice, 2 fill in the blank, 1 true or false.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: All of stop 2 (6:50-81) is a repeated Aaron genealogy plus land and town lists. That is a long stretch, but it has a stop of its own instead of one summary story card in a stop with the moments around it.

rule.text: A stretch never gets a stop of its own. Its one card sits in the stop with the moments around it.

findings.problem: Cards 2, 4, 5 and 7 are choice cards about the town list long stretch: the first lot, Caleb getting Hebron's fields, Hebron's pasturelands, and who gave the cities. The Hebron and Caleb detail is a short story inside the stretch. It can be the standout detail on the summary card, but it shouldn't get choice cards.

rule.text: A short story inside the stretch, like Nimrod in the list of nations (Genesis 10:8–12), is part of the stretch: it can be the standout detail on that card, but it gets no choice cards.

findings.problem: This regular story card has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 3 multiple choice, 1 true or false, no fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card says 'Then the cities get named tribe by tribe, from Judah and Ephraim...' for 6:65-81. The text names Judah's cities earlier (6:55-60). Verse 65 only refers back to 'the cities named above,' so Judah's cities are not named again in this stretch.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card calls Shechem 'a city of refuge too,' but no earlier card told the baker that Hebron is a city of refuge (6:57). Without that, 'too' doesn't make sense.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
